In GoogleCalendarService.createEvent the target calendar is now chosen solely via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`, falling back to `"primary"`. In EventManager's else-branch (`} else { const destinationCalendarCredentials = this.calendarCredentials.filter((c) => c.type === destination.integration); ... await createEvent(c, event))`), destinations without a credentialId are served by calling createEvent once per matching credential with no externalId, so the find never matches and the event goes to each credential's primary calendar — a behavior change from the pre-diff code, which used `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.externalId` directly regardless of credentialId. The resulting reference stores `result.externalId` (the passed, possibly-undefined externalId), which reschedule/cancel paths (`handleCancelBooking`, `updateEvent`) depend on. judged_text: createEvent now selects the target calendar solely via destinationCalendar.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId), so a destination calendar without a credentialId — the case EventManager's else-branch exists to serve — never matches and the event is written to 'primary' instead of the destination's configured externalId. Bookings against a credentialId-less destination calendar now land in each connected Google credential's primary calendar (duplicating the event once per credential) instead of the user's selected calendar, and the stored reference ends up with a wrong or missing externalCalendarId that later reschedule/cancel paths depend on.

adjudication.rationale: In `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent`, the target calendar is now chosen by `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` and falls back to `"primary"` when no match is found. In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, the else-branch explicitly handles destinations without `credentialId` by iterating matching credentials (`c.type === destination.integration`) and calling `createEvent(c, event)` **without** passing `destination.externalId` (the new `externalId?` arg in `CalendarManager.createEvent`). As a result, for destination calendar entries that lack `credentialId`, Google calendar inserts will not use the configured `externalId` and will write to `primary` for each matched credential. Also, because `CalendarManager.createEvent` returns `externalId` from the passed argument and the else-branch passes none, `result.externalId` becomes `undefined`, leading to missing/wrong `externalCalendarId` later (EventManager now sets `externalCalendarId: result.externalId`).
